subject: Dedicated capacity: acceptance criteria, SLOs, and ramp plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediquant.com>, Sofia Perez <sofia.perez@mediquant.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: acceptance criteria, SLOs, and ramp plan

Alex / Sofia,

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion and appreciate the transparency on traffic shapes and compliance needs. This note captures the call outcomes and the proposed path forward so we have alignment before we put together the formal proposal.

High-level pain / goals you shared:
- Latency-sensitive inference (avg P95 target ~120ms) for returned recommendations across 128-token context windows.
- Multi-tenant concerns: need tenant isolation for PHI/PII workloads and strong auditability of inference logs.
- Predictable throughput during marketing spikes (3x baseline for 6-8 hours/day).

Redwood recommended architecture (dedicated capacity):
- Reserved GPU pool (2 x A100-80GB equiv nodes to start) with tenant-segmentation: dedicated namespaces + KV prefix isolation.
- Burst policy: pre-allocated burst bucket for scheduled spikes, fallback to queued capacity for unplanned surges.
- SLAs: target P95 latency <= 120ms, availability SLA request (we discussed 99.5% monthly) — draft attached.

Acceptance criteria we will use to agree on go/no-go:
1) Throughput validation: demo run hitting 2k concurrent requests at your peak query size, measured P50/P95/P99.
2) Isolation verification: audit of tenant access controls, KMS integration, and export of sample audit logs.
3) Failover: automated fallback to smaller quantized model variant with <2x latency increase and preserved correctness on smoke prompts.

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood: produce a capacity estimate + SLA draft (attachment) and a proposal with pricing bands for base reserved pool + burst. (Owner: me) — ETA Wed 11/12.
- MediQuant: share production traffic histogram for Q3 weekdays and the legal contact for procurement/managed contract review. (Owner: Alex / procurement) — ETA Fri 11/13.
- Ops deep-dive: technical call to validate KV-cache behavior and quantization tolerance with your ML infra team. (Owner: Ben) — propose 11/16 or 11/17.

Attachments: SLA_Draft_v0.2.pdf, capacity-estimate-mediquant.csv attached for your review.

If that aligns, we’ll convert this into a mutual action plan and lock in times for the Ops deep-dive.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediquant.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Perez <sofia.perez@mediquant.com>, procurement@mediquant.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: acceptance criteria, SLOs, and ramp plan

Rachel — great summary, thank you.

Quick answers / clarifications: 
- We can share the traffic histogram; I’ll have Sofia pull the last 90 days and include percentile breakdowns.
- Legal will need the SLA to start review; procurement@mediquant.com is looped.
- For the Ops deep-dive, 11/16 at 11am PT works for our infra lead (Victor).

Two questions from my side:
1) For the burst policy you mentioned, what is the expected cold-start behavior for a model variant switch? In particular we need to understand how long the quantized fallback will take to respond under load.
2) Can you confirm the audit log retention default and whether we can set it to 12 months for PHI-related endpoints?

Thanks — I’ll upload the traffic histogram by EOD 11/13.

– Alex
Head of ML Ops, MediQuant

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediquant.com>, Sofia Perez <sofia.perez@mediquant.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: acceptance criteria, SLOs, and ramp plan

Alex — thanks, that schedule works. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) cold-start behavior for model variant switch?
We designed the fallback path with warm standby quantized variants for common models — switching is sub-second for KV cache hits, and typically 1.5–3s for cold KV misses depending on sequence length. For your profile (128 tokens) expect ~2s during first few requests; after that P95 settles close to the target. We’ll validate this in the Ops run.

> 2) audit log retention default and ability to set 12 months?
Yes — default is 90 days in hosted, but in Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and connect to your KMS. Setting to 12 months for PHI endpoints is supported; we’ll include this in the MOP and the contract addendum.

I’ve attached an updated MOP checklist that maps the acceptance criteria to measurable test cases. Ben — can you prepare the load script and the initial quantized-model smoke prompts (I’ll share a seed prompt set with Alex)?

Rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediquant.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: acceptance criteria, SLOs, and ramp plan

Looping in a short checklist from Ops side based on what we’ll validate on 11/16 deep-dive:
- Load script: synthetic traffic generator configured to mirror provided histogram (90m run at peak QPS).
- Latency measurement: P50/P95/P99 with and without KV cache warm-up; record token-level timing.
- Isolation test: simultaneous multi-tenant traffic with tenant A running PHI prompts and tenant B running baseline requests; verify no cross-tenant KV leakage.
- Failover test: toggle routing policy to quantized fallback under simulated instance drain and measure response curvature.

Attachments: MOP_Checklist.xlsx (updated), capacity-estimate-mediquant.csv (baseline numbers).

Ben Carter
Director, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Sofia Perez <sofia.perez@mediquant.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediquant.com>, procurement@mediquant.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: acceptance criteria, SLOs, and ramp plan

Thanks all — confirmed on our side. Procurement will review the SLA_Draft_v0.2.pdf and follow up with redlines; Victor will be on the Ops deep-dive 11/16.

Mutual action plan (confirmed):
- 11/12: Redwood sends full proposal & updated SLA (Rachel) — complete.
- 11/13: MediQuant shares traffic histogram & legal contact (Alex / procurement) — pending (Sofia to confirm EOD).
- 11/16: Ops deep-dive (Ben / Victor) — confirmed 11am PT.
- 11/19: Redwood provides final capacity reservation quote and draft SOW based on validation tests.

We’d like to prioritize a short trial window (2 weeks) after validation before committing to a 12-month reserved pool. Is that acceptable?

Best,
Sofia Perez
Senior Product Manager, MediQuant
sofia.perez@mediquant.com
